column1: # Source suffix | Fresh context | Correct contextual paraphrase | Distractor | Distractor | Clue

001|The small charity attracted volunteers at an astonishing rate.|Volunteers joined surprisingly quickly.|Volunteers joined at a predictable, steady pace.|Volunteers stopped joining entirely.|Consider what surprised the organisers about the speed.

002|The lake became increasingly polluted over several summers.|The pollution grew worse over time.|The pollution stayed at exactly the same level.|The pollution disappeared completely.|Compare the degree of pollution from one summer to the next.

003|By noon, the narrow market lanes were congested.|People could barely move through the crowded lanes.|The lanes had been permanently closed for repairs.|The lanes were almost empty.|Think about how easily someone could move there.

004|The school planned an expansion of its science facilities.|It planned to make the facilities larger.|It planned to close all science facilities.|It planned to repaint them without changing their size.|Focus on the size of the facilities.

005|The planners chose an overground railway for the new district.|The trains would travel above ground.|The trains would travel in deep tunnels.|The trains would be replaced by buses.|Consider where the tracks would run.

006|A network of footpaths connects the villages.|Several linked paths connect different places.|One isolated path serves a single house.|Every path is separate from all the others.|Look at how the paths relate to one another.

007|Skipping maintenance may result in costly repairs.|Skipping it may cause expensive repairs later.|Skipping it will prevent all repair costs.|The repairs have no connection to maintenance.|Look for a cause and its consequence.

008|Each passenger had to show a ticket before boarding.|Each person travelling on the service needed a ticket.|Only the vehicle's mechanic needed a ticket.|Only the person selling tickets needed a ticket.|Focus on who is making the journey.

009|The delegation travelled to the capital to meet national officials.|It travelled to the country's main city.|It travelled to a factory's financial office.|It travelled to the country's smallest village.|Here the word names a place, rather than money.

011|The agreement was a historic moment for the island.|It was important in the island's history.|It was a fictional story set in the past.|It was an ordinary event with no lasting significance.|Consider the event's importance, not simply its age.

012|The audience stood around the performer to form a ring.|They arranged themselves in a circle.|They formed a straight line behind the stage.|They all stood on one side of the performer.|Picture the audience's arrangement.

013|The toolkit consists of six basic instruments.|Six instruments make up the toolkit.|Six instruments are missing from the toolkit.|The toolkit is used to manufacture six instruments.|Consider what is inside the complete set.

014|The poorly built shed leaked during its first storm.|The shed's construction was of low quality.|The shed was expensive but carefully made.|The shed had simply become too old.|Its age is not the reason given for the leak.

015|The clinic's waiting room was overcrowded on Monday.|It held more people than it could comfortably accommodate.|It had plenty of empty seats for everyone.|Its opening hours were too short.|Think about people relative to the available space.

016|The housing survey examined conditions in a slum.|It examined a poor urban area with crowded, inadequate housing.|It examined an expensive residential estate.|It examined an uninhabited stretch of farmland.|Consider both housing conditions and the urban setting.

017|Visitors toured the village in a horse-drawn cart.|A horse pulled the cart.|A motor pushed the cart along a rail.|The visitors carried the cart themselves.|Identify what provides the pulling force.

018|The cancelled ferry turned their journey into a nightmare.|The journey became an extremely unpleasant experience.|They fell asleep and imagined the entire journey.|The journey became unusually relaxing.|The expression is figurative in this travel context.

019|Passengers left their bags in the railway carriage.|They left them in a compartment or coach of the train.|They left them in the station's ticket office.|They left them beside the track outside the train.|Here the setting is a train, rather than a horse-drawn vehicle.
020|Numerous residents attended the safety meeting.|A large number of residents attended.|Only one resident attended.|No residents attended.|Focus on the number of people.

021|The council introduced a scheme to improve street lighting.|It introduced an organised improvement plan.|It reported an accidental failure of the lights.|It announced the completion of every planned repair.|Consider whether this describes a plan or an accident.

022|The engineers will propose a safer crossing.|They will put forward an idea for consideration.|They will reject every possible crossing.|They will confirm the crossing has already been built.|The decision has not yet been made.

023|The new timetable should resolve the scheduling conflict.|It should solve the conflict.|It should create a new conflict deliberately.|It should hide the conflict without addressing it.|Think about the intended effect on the problem.
024|With careful preparation, the team hoped to succeed.|It hoped to achieve its goal.|It hoped to withdraw before starting.|It hoped to change its name.|Focus on the desired result of its work.

025|Rina became a vocal advocate for safer playgrounds.|She spoke actively in support of safer playgrounds.|She quietly opposed all playground improvements.|She was hired only to inspect playground equipment.|Consider her public position on the proposal.

026|A buyer in England asked a solicitor to handle the property paperwork.|The buyer sought help from a legal professional.|The buyer hired a builder to repair the roof.|The buyer hired a reporter to publish the sale.|Think about the professional expertise needed for legal paperwork.

027|The report highlighted the social and economic advantages of the park.|It described benefits for the community and the economy.|It described only the park's colours and shapes.|It described only the project's social and financial costs.|Consider who or what benefits.

028|The bridge will link together two walking trails.|It will connect trails that were separate.|It will remove both trails completely.|It will keep walkers permanently apart.|Think about the relationship between the trails after construction.

029|The redevelopment plan aimed to clear slums.|It aimed to remove areas of poor-quality housing.|It aimed only to wash the streets without changing housing.|It aimed to build more overcrowded housing.|This refers to removing housing, rather than routine cleaning.
030|The studio will relocate to another district.|It will move to a different place.|It will close permanently without reopening.|It will remain at its current address.|Look for a change of location.

031|The charity opened an inner-city youth centre.|It opened a centre in a central urban area.|It opened a centre in remote countryside.|It opened a centre beyond the city's outer suburbs.|Consider the centre's location within the city.

032|The team inspected a newly constructed bridge.|The bridge had been built recently.|The bridge was merely proposed on paper.|The bridge had stood unchanged for centuries.|Focus on when construction took place.

033|The family moved to a quiet suburb outside the busy centre.|It moved to an outlying residential area.|It moved into the city's central business square.|It moved to an isolated ocean island.|Consider its relationship to the city centre.

034|The centre will provide free helmets for the cycling course.|It will make helmets available to participants.|It will forbid participants from wearing helmets.|It will require participants to manufacture helmets.|Focus on what the centre supplies.

035|The campaign began to gain support among local shopkeepers.|More shopkeepers began backing it.|More shopkeepers began opposing it.|Shopkeepers stopped hearing about it entirely.|Consider the change in people's approval.

036|The architect must submit a plan before work starts.|The architect must officially present the plan for consideration.|The architect must destroy the plan.|The architect must complete the building without a plan.|Think about the approval process before construction.

037|The committee decided to reject the application.|It refused to accept the application.|It approved the application immediately.|It asked the applicant to sign an already approved permit.|Focus on whether permission was given.

038|The arts festival will coincide with the school holidays.|The two events will happen at the same time.|The festival will happen years before the holidays.|The festival will cause the holidays to be cancelled.|Compare the timing of the two events.

039|The board discussed a proposal for a shared garden.|It discussed a suggested plan.|It inspected a garden already completed under a contract.|It counted the existing garden's flowers.|Consider whether the idea is still being considered.

040|After the debate, the council voted to pass the proposal.|It officially approved the proposal.|It refused to consider the proposal.|It accidentally lost the proposal's documents.|Here pass refers to a formal decision.

041|The two community groups agreed to merge.|They agreed to combine into one organisation.|They agreed to separate into smaller groups.|They agreed to compete without sharing resources.|Consider the number of organisations afterwards.

042|The graduates hope to establish a research centre.|They hope to formally set up a centre.|They hope to close an existing centre.|They hope to visit a centre for one afternoon.|Think about bringing an organisation into existence.

043|Volunteers will construct a shelter beside the trail.|They will build the shelter.|They will demolish the shelter.|They will draw a map of a distant shelter.|Consider the physical work being planned.

044|The club held events to raise funding for a new roof.|It tried to obtain money for the roof.|It tried to spend all its remaining money elsewhere.|It tried to increase the roof's height.|Here raise concerns financial resources.

045|The architect suggested a radical redesign of the library.|The redesign differed greatly from conventional approaches.|The redesign repeated the old layout exactly.|The redesign changed only one door handle.|Consider how far the idea departs from the familiar.

046|The route was popular, not least because of its coastal views.|The views were a particularly important reason for its popularity.|The views were irrelevant to its popularity.|The views were the least attractive feature of the route.|The phrase emphasises a reason rather than dismissing it.

047|The review was critical of the plan's lack of wheelchair access.|It expressed disapproval of that omission.|It praised the plan's accessibility without reservation.|It described an emergency medical condition.|Here critical concerns the reviewer's opinion.

048|The announcement attracted attention from the press.|Newspapers and other news media paid attention.|A printing machine physically moved towards it.|A group of athletes pressed a button.|Consider who reports public announcements.

049|An objector spoke against the proposed car park.|A person opposing the plan spoke.|A person funding the plan promised more money.|A person officially approving the plan signed it.|Focus on the speaker's position towards the plan.

050|Researchers argue that shaded streets improve comfort.|They present reasons for that view.|They physically fight over ownership of the streets.|They refuse to express any view.|In this context, argue concerns reasoning.

051|The weakened wall could collapse in strong winds.|It could suddenly fall down.|It could gradually become taller.|It could safely move to another site intact.|Consider the risk created by a weakened structure.

052|Workers checked the cables overhead.|They checked cables above them.|They checked cables buried under their feet.|They calculated their office's operating expenses.|Here overhead describes a physical position.
053|Passing trucks made the windows shake.|The windows vibrated rapidly.|The windows opened and stayed motionless.|The windows became completely opaque.|Focus on movement caused by the trucks.

054|A chemical leak could poison the fish in the pond.|It could harm the fish through a toxic substance.|It could provide extra food safely.|It could move the fish to a new pond.|Consider the effect of a harmful chemical.

055|The factory installed filters to reduce smoke emissions.|It aimed to release less smoke into the air.|It aimed to employ fewer factory workers.|It aimed to increase the amount of raw material delivered.|Think about substances leaving the factory.

056|Despite several failed trials, the inventors persisted.|They continued trying despite difficulties.|They abandoned the project immediately.|They denied having started the project.|Consider their response to setbacks.
057|The ramp will enable wheelchair users to reach the stage.|It will make access possible.|It will prevent access.|It will remove the stage entirely.|Focus on what becomes possible.

058|The cooperative decided to invest in better equipment.|It put money into equipment for future benefit.|It refused to spend any money on equipment.|It sold all equipment and stopped operating.|Consider how the money is being used.

059|After months of repairs, the gallery eventually reopened.|It reopened in the end, after a period of time.|It reopened before any repairs began.|It reopened repeatedly every hour.|Look at its position in the sequence of events.

060|The driver checked the route to the campsite.|The driver checked which path to follow.|The driver checked the vehicle's ownership papers.|The driver checked the passengers' meals.|Think about navigation.
061|A storage chamber lies beneath the main hall.|It is underneath the hall.|It is above the hall's roof.|It is beside the hall at the same height.|Compare the vertical positions.

062|Reusable containers help minimise packaging waste.|They help reduce waste as far as possible.|They help increase waste deliberately.|They guarantee waste is always exactly one kilogram.|The aim is reduction, without a fixed numerical promise.

063|The additional expense made the repairs difficult to afford.|The extra cost caused difficulty.|The extra income made everything free.|The extra time had no financial effect.|Focus on money that must be paid.

064|The owners obtained permission to demolish the unsafe garage.|They could deliberately tear it down.|They could preserve it without any changes.|They could move it intact to another street.|Consider what will happen to the structure itself.

065|The concert was originally scheduled for Friday, then moved to Sunday.|Friday was the first planned date.|Sunday had always been the only planned date.|The concert was never given a date.|Distinguish the initial plan from the revised one.

066|Construction of the health centre began in spring.|Building work began then.|Medical treatment began in the completed centre.|Demolition of the completed centre ended then.|Focus on the building process.

067|The entrance is at street level.|It is at the same height as the road surface.|It is on the roof several floors above the road.|It is deep below the road.|Compare the entrance height with the road.

068|The gardener demonstrated a technique for planting seedlings.|The gardener showed a method.|The gardener listed only the plants' prices.|The gardener named the owner of the garden.|Consider how the task is performed.

069|Engineers chose cut and cover for the shallow tunnel.|They would dig an open trench, build the tunnel, then cover it.|They would bore a deep tunnel without opening the surface.|They would build only a bridge above the road.|Think about the sequence of opening and closing the ground.
070|Workers dug a trench for the drainage pipe.|They dug a long, narrow excavation.|They built a tall, solid tower.|They laid a flat sheet on untouched ground.|Picture the shape of the excavation.

071|The library is temporarily using the school hall.|It is using the hall for a limited period.|It has bought the hall for permanent use.|It has never used the hall.|Consider whether this arrangement will last indefinitely.

072|Steel props hold up the damaged ceiling.|They physically support the ceiling.|They delay the start of a meeting.|They pull the ceiling down deliberately.|Here hold up describes structural support.

073|A timber beam supports the roof above the doorway.|A long wooden structural support carries the load.|A plastic pipe supplies water to the roof.|A loose fabric sheet covers the doorway.|Think about both the material and its structural job.

074|A brick arch spans the entrance to the courtyard.|A curved structure made of bricks crosses the entrance.|A flat wooden door blocks the courtyard.|A metal pipe runs below the entrance.|Consider the shape and building material.

075|The worker spread a thin layer of sand over the surface.|The worker added a thickness of material on top.|The worker removed the entire underlying surface.|The worker dug one deep hole in the centre.|Picture material covering a surface.

076|After the storm, residents helped rebuild the community hall.|They helped construct it again.|They helped abandon it permanently.|They helped rename it without repairing it.|The prefix indicates doing the building again.

077|The ferry returned to normal operation after repairs.|The transport service was functioning normally again.|A surgical procedure had begun on the ferry.|The ferry was only being designed on paper.|Here operation concerns a service functioning.

078|The planned railway extension would reach two more villages.|An addition to the railway would serve more places.|The existing line would become shorter.|The railway would close all existing stations.|Think about adding to an existing system.

079|Only the manager can authorise the purchase.|Only the manager can give official permission.|Only the manager can deliver the purchased goods.|Only the manager can object without making a decision.|Focus on the authority to approve.

080|The museum restored a steam locomotive for demonstration runs.|It restored a train engine powered by steam.|It restored an electric bus.|It restored a train carriage with no engine.|Identify the vehicle and its power source.

081|The boiler heats water to produce steam for the engine.|The equipment turns heated water into steam.|The equipment stores cold fuel without heating it.|The equipment cools steam into ice.|Focus on the equipment's heating function.

082|The clinic will introduce a new booking system next month.|It will bring the system into use.|It will withdraw the system permanently.|It will simply mention an old system in a history lesson.|Consider the system entering practical use.

083|The classrooms will be fitted with air filters.|Air filters will be installed in them.|Air filters will be removed from them.|The classrooms will manufacture filters for sale.|Think about what equipment the rooms will have.

084|Water vapour will condense on the cold glass.|The vapour will change into liquid.|The vapour will turn liquid water into gas.|The glass will turn into a gas.|Consider the direction of the change in state.

085|Workers opened the doors to let paint fumes escape.|They let strong vapours from the paint leave.|They let solid paintbrushes leave on their own.|They let clean drinking water flow in.|Think about what can remain in the air after painting.

086|A ventilation shaft brings fresh air into the underground room.|A passage allows air to circulate.|A pipe supplies only drinking water.|A sealed pillar prevents all air movement.|Focus on airflow through a passage.

087|The morning congestion added twenty minutes to the journey.|Heavy traffic delayed the journey.|An empty road allowed unusually fast travel.|A lower ticket price delayed the journey.|Consider what slows road traffic.

088|The walking circuit returns hikers to the starting point.|The route forms a loop.|The route ends far away and never returns.|The route is a single isolated step.|Here circuit describes the shape of a route.

089|Cycling is an alternative to taking the bus.|Cycling is another available option.|Cycling is the only compulsory choice.|Cycling is identical to riding the bus.|Think about having a choice between methods.

090|The inspection took place in a confined space under the floor.|The area was small and enclosed.|The area was a wide, open field.|The area was crowded only because of a public festival.|Consider the physical limits of the area itself.

091|The rescue team needs reliable radios.|It needs radios that work dependably.|It needs radios that fail unpredictably.|It needs radios selected only for their colour.|Think about being able to depend on the equipment.

092|An electric motor drives the small workshop lift.|A motor powered by electricity moves it.|A horse pulls it using a rope.|A steam engine burns coal to move it.|Identify the source of the motor's power.

093|The island receives supplies by means of a small boat.|A boat is the method used to deliver supplies.|The boat is the reason supplies are no longer needed.|The boat is the destination where all supplies stay.|Here means refers to a method, rather than a definition.

094|The cable can transfer power from the battery to the lamp.|It can transmit energy between the devices.|It can move the whole battery into the lamp.|It can remove the lamp's need for any energy.|Distinguish moving energy from moving a physical device.

095|A portable generator kept the lights on during the outage.|A device produced electricity.|A container stored drinking water.|A machine removed all electricity from the building.|Focus on the production of electrical power.

096|The city proposed a deep-level electric railway.|It proposed an electric line far below the surface.|It proposed a horse-drawn line on the road.|It proposed a steam railway on an elevated bridge.|Both the location and power source matter.
097|The display is made up of six separate panels.|Six panels compose the display.|Six panels have been removed from the display.|The display manufactures six panels.|Consider the parts of the whole.
098|The narrow doorway made furniture delivery difficult.|The doorway was not wide.|The doorway was unusually wide.|The doorway was far above the roof.|Focus on width.

099|A damaged cable interrupted the building's power supply.|It interrupted the provision of electricity.|It interrupted the delivery of office furniture.|It interrupted the flow of drinking water.|Consider what the cable carries.

100|The reusable spacecraft was described as a technical achievement.|It was a successful technological accomplishment.|It was only a change in ticket prices.|It was a natural event with no engineering involved.|Focus on successful technology or engineering.

101|The bakery hopes to make a profit this year.|It hopes to earn more than it spends.|It hopes its costs will exceed its income.|It hopes to give away every product without income.|Compare income with expenditure.

102|A new safety procedure is now in place.|The procedure is established and functioning.|The procedure is merely an unapproved suggestion.|The procedure has been permanently abandoned.|Consider whether the arrangement is actually operating.

103|The talk ended, and the workshop began soon afterwards.|The workshop began a short time after the talk.|The workshop began long before the talk.|The workshop began at an unspecified date years later.|Look at the order and the short interval.
